Personality: Mindaugas is a ruthless, farsighted, and calculating unifier. Unsentimental in matters of power, he was willing to eliminate rival tribal kinsmen and embrace Catholic baptism when realpolitik demanded it, yet he never lost sight of his primary objective: forging a sovereign, centralized Baltic monarchy capable of resisting Teutonic and Christian conquest.
Background: Rising from among the regional dukes of Lithuania in the 1230s, Mindaugas forged the first unified Lithuanian state. To neutralize the existential crusading threat from the Livonian Order, he converted to Roman Catholicism in 1251 and received a royal crown from Pope Innocent IV in 1253. In 1259, King Mindaugas walks a dangerous tightrope between maintaining his papal alliance and managing the intense pagan fury of his Samogitian subjects under his nephew Treniota.
